## 929a3e437ee4

**Classification: reproduced semantic domain gap / suspected shortcut, not an in-domain execution defect.** Generator SHA-256: `a187a88c3a47215c5ea74928f3dcea6327074e01724eb2b62154d65a13b089f0`; executed rule hash: `7cfafaaa1f5f`.

The intended rule selects colors by **total cell count**. The generator’s invariant and self-check require every nonzero color to form exactly one 4-connected object. Under that restriction, total color count equals largest connected-component count, so generated lessons cannot distinguish this plausible rival:

> Select the color(s) whose largest 4-connected component is largest, then apply the same leftmost ordering/output construction.

`checks/audit/929a3e437ee4/input.json` supplies an exact 10×10 witness: color `2` has six cells split into two 3-cell components, while color `8` has one 5-cell component. The supported `arcpuzzles apply` command records the authoritative Racket output as a 6×1 bar of color `2` in `racket.json`. The rival produces a 5×1 bar of color `8`; both outputs and counts are stored in `counterexample.json`.

This witness is **outside the documented generator domain** and fails the target self-check with `color 2 must form one 4-connected object`. That is the point of the audit: the single-component restriction is a distributional blind spot that prevents the lessons from teaching total-count semantics. It is not evidence that the Racket rule or generated in-domain labels are wrong.

The shared semantic gate also warns rather than passes because the generator declares several witness predicates but no rival claim; see `checks/audit/929a3e437ee4/semantic_gate/`. A repair could either generate controlled multi-component same-color cases or explicitly declare/test the largest-component rival while relaxing the invariant. The target source was left unchanged.

## 929a3e437ee4

**AUDIT-929-F1 — Reproduced distributional shortcut on current source; target left unchanged.** Current generator SHA-256: `a187a88c3a47215c5ea74928f3dcea6327074e01724eb2b62154d65a13b089f0`; executed rule hash: `7cfafaaa1f5f`.

The authority selects colors by **total cell count**, but the generator and `self_check` require every color to form one 4-connected object. Therefore every generated lesson makes total count identical to largest-component count and cannot refute the plausible rival “select the color whose largest 4-connected component is largest, then use the same output construction.”

`checks/audit/929a3e437ee4/counterexample.json` retains an exact 10×10 witness. Color 2 has total count 6 split into two 3-cell components; color 8 has total count 5 in one component. Supported Racket `apply` returns a 6×1 bar of color 2, while the rival returns a 5×1 bar of color 8. The witness is intentionally outside the documented generator domain and `self_check` rejects it with `color 2 must form one 4-connected object`; this is a teaching-distribution gap, not a bad Racket label. The same issue was already unresolved in the target’s review index, and the source hash is unchanged; this audit independently re-ran the current authority in `checks/audit/929a3e437ee4/racket.json`.
